action_items: None blocking — the pivoted spec is fully met and every listed test bullet passed.

OPTIONAL: The RichTextEditor uses document.execCommand which is deprecated (already noted in the source docstring). If cross-browser fidelity ever becomes an issue, migrate to a modern editor (TipTap / Slate). Current implementation works fine in Chromium.

OPTIONAL: The RTE has no visible placeholder text when empty — the JSX comment mentions a .rte-empty class trick but there's no CSS rule for it. Consider adding a `:empty::before { content: attr(data-placeholder); ... }` for a11y hint.

OPTIONAL (carryover from iter 4): server.py is ~970 lines now (grew from 890) — split into routers/ modules is overdue. Same applies to the CSRF-cookie regex duplication in NotificationEmailView.onImport (fetch is used instead of apiFetch because of multipart).
critical_code_review_comments: server.py::notification_send stores the ENTIRE html_template in the history row's `pdf` blob column (up to 16 KB), duplicating what's in `summary`. Fine for now but if operators send large HTML repeatedly, consider streaming to a separate collection or dropping the blob for notification-type entries.

server.py::notification_send does NOT sanitize/limit CC list length beyond Field(max_length=20). Non-admin misuse is impossible today (require_auth) but if this endpoint ever opens up, a malicious admin could still spray up to 20*500=10k emails per batch. Not a bug for the current threat model, just worth flagging.

The per-recipient `.replace('{{name}}', ...).replace('{name}', ...)` scheme is applied to the RAW HTML — if a recipient's name contains an angle bracket, it will be injected verbatim into the HTML and render as (probably-benign) text. Since names come from the seeded roster (trusted source), OK for now, but if the roster ever accepts free-text names from an untrusted source, wrap the name in `html.escape(...)` before replacement.

The 3rd param to `document.execCommand('createLink', url)` in RichTextEditor accepts the raw user prompt value — a `javascript:` URL would be inserted as-is. execCommand actually blocks `javascript:` in most modern browsers, but consider a startsWith('http') / mailto: whitelist for defence in depth.

NotificationEmailView.onImport still parses `document.cookie` for the CSRF token instead of using the same helper `apiFetch`/`apiJSON` uses (same finding as iter 4). Duplicate logic across the codebase — small refactor opportunity.

The RTE reset flow depends on `resetKey` being bumped by the parent, but the initial value on mount is also driven by the `value` prop through the same effect (`if (lastReset.current !== resetKey || ref.current.innerHTML === '')`). If a parent ever mounts with a non-empty value and then bumps resetKey without changing value, the editor correctly resets — good. However, if the parent passes value=<changing string> without bumping resetKey, changes to value silently do NOT sync to the DOM (by design, to avoid caret jumps). Documented in the source comment; just be aware.
